title: Coherent scalar-extension diagrams for a fixed finitely presented module arrow
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed preorder, $A_i$ a diagram of commutative rings with transitions $a_{ji}:A_i\to A_j$ and ring-colimit cocone $\kappa_i:A_i\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $c\in I$, finitely presented $A_c$-modules $P,Q$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], and an $A_c$-linear map $v:P\to Q$. For $j\ge c$ put $P_j=P\otimes_{A_c}A_j$, $Q_j=Q\otimes_{A_c}A_j$, $v_j=v\otimes1$, and put $P_A=P\otimes_{A_c}A$, $Q_A=Q\otimes_{A_c}A$, $v_A=v\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For $c\le j\le k$ specify
$p_{kj}(x\otimes a)=x\otimes a_{kj}(a)$, $q_{kj}(y\otimes a)=y\otimes a_{kj}(a)$,
$\mu_j(x\otimes a)=x\otimes\kappa_j(a)$, and $\nu_j(y\otimes a)=y\otimes\kappa_j(a)$.
These formulas define additive maps semilinear over the corresponding ring maps. They obey identities, composition, cocone compatibility, $q_{kj}v_j=v_kp_{kj}$ and $\nu_jv_j=v_A\mu_j$. Every $P_j,Q_j$ is finitely presented. The canonical $A_k$-linear maps $P_j\otimes_{A_j}A_k\to P_k$, $z\otimes b\mapsto b\,p_{kj}(z)$, and $Q_j\otimes_{A_j}A_k\to Q_k$, $z\otimes b\mapsto b\,q_{kj}(z)$, are isomorphisms. The canonical $A$-linear maps $P_j\otimes_{A_j}A\to P_A$, $z\otimes b\mapsto b\,\mu_j(z)$, and $Q_j\otimes_{A_j}A\to Q_A$, $z\otimes b\mapsto b\,\nu_j(z)$, are isomorphisms. Both pairs intertwine the scalar extensions of $v_j$ with $v_k$ and $v_A$, respectively. The specified cocones exhibit $P_A$ and $Q_A$ as colimits of the underlying abelian groups on the directed tail $I_{\ge c}$. Every element of either limit module is represented at one stage, and two stage elements have equal images exactly when their images agree at a common later stage. The tail is small, nonempty and directed. These assertions allow zero modules, the zero map, empty finite presentations and rings with zero divisors; no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on any $A_i$ is imposed. All sets may lie in a common sufficiently large universe.

proof.text: The upper tail J = I≥c contains c and is directed by taking an upper bound in I. Its inclusion F is final: every i has an upper bound with c, and parallel maps in the preorder agree. Apply Mathlib Functor.final_of_exists_of_isFiltered and Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv to restrict the given ring colimit. This is the filtered dual of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory].

proof.text: For a ring triangle R→S→T whose composite is h, Mathlib ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp gives the scalarComparison isomorphism T⊗S(S⊗R P) ≅ T⊗R P. Define scalarTransition by the scalar-extension unit z↦1⊗z followed by this comparison. The unit and restricted comparison give semilinearity. The comparison on nested unit tensors gives scalarTransition(a⊗x)=g(a)⊗x. Apply this to stage transitions and cocone legs. Tensor induction, ring functoriality and cocone naturality prove identity, composition and compatibility, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), balanced presentation; explicit verification of the fixed-stage construction used in Tag 00QX

proof.text: For any $R$-algebra $B$, the formula $v_B(x\otimes b)=v(x)\otimes b$ is well defined by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], since $v$ is $R$-linear. It is $B$-linear by multiplication in the second factor. On $x\otimes a\in P_j$, both $q_{kj}v_j$ and $v_kp_{kj}$ have value $v(x)\otimes a_{kj}(a)$, and both $\nu_jv_j$ and $v_A\mu_j$ have value $v(x)\otimes\kappa_j(a)$. Equality follows on all elements by additive generation. Thus the constructed diagrams form the stated arrow diagram.

source.place: Tags 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), first paragraph: simultaneous module arrows

proof.text: For each stage equip B(j) with its B(c)-algebra structure from the specified ring map. Mathlib instFinitePresentationTensorProduct (Mathlib.Algebra.Module.FinitePresentation) directly supplies finite presentation of B(j)⊗B(c) T for T=P,Q. This is exactly the carrier and module structure of fixedArrowStage. The instance implements the ordinary finite-presentation argument of [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] and works for zero modules, empty presentations and arbitrary ring maps.

Use scalarComparison from Step 2 for each stage and limit ring triangle. For any z and b its linearity identifies the value on b⊗z with b times its value on 1⊗z, which is b times scalarTransition(z) by construction. Thus these are the specified canonical comparison isomorphisms of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], not arbitrary isomorphisms.

proof.text: Prove scalarTransition_natural by tensor induction: on a⊗x, both sides equal g(a)⊗v(x). For scalarComparison_natural use Mathlib ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.hom_ext, which reduces to tensors 1⊗z; these give the previously proved transition naturality. This establishes the stage and limit arrow squares and both comparison intertwining identities, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: Build the additive functor D from the stage transitions and its cocone δ from the limit legs. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-diagram-elementwise] on the upper tail using the ring colimit from Step 1, semilinearity from Step 2 and the linear equivalences underlying the comparisons of Step 5. All tensors already have the cited theorem’s ring-first convention. It yields representatives and eventual zero. To prove the common-stage equality criterion, move two representatives to an upper bound, apply eventual zero to their difference, and use functoriality; the reverse implication is cocone naturality.

source.place: Tags 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit), 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit), 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits), as encapsulated by the cited elementwise comparison node

proof.text: To prove the colimit in abelian groups, take any abelian group $H$ and compatible additive maps $f_j:T_j\to H$. Step 7 allows the definition $f(\tau_j(z))=f_j(z)$ on all of $T_A$. It is well defined because equal representatives agree at a common later stage and compatibility makes their $f_j$-values equal. To check additivity, move representatives $z\in T_j$ and $w\in T_k$ to a common $\ell\ge j,k$; then $f(\tau_j(z)+\tau_k(w))=f_\ell(t_{\ell j}z+t_{\ell k}w)=f_j(z)+f_k(w)$. A zero representative gives $f(0)=0$. Thus $f$ is additive and $f\tau_j=f_j$. Representation of every element forces uniqueness. This is exactly the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in abelian groups. Apply it for $T=P$ and for $T=Q$. All constructions use additive and balancing relations, right exactness and directedness only; neither cancellation in a ring, nonzero modules, positive presentation sizes, flatness nor a Noetherian hypothesis was used.
